title: Ideal-nest blueprint candidates (vertical section, body-length units)

tags.WS: web-search summary only, page not opened
tags.ASSUMED: design choice where the literature gave no number

units.x: columns from the entrance centre in BL, + = right
units.depth: rows below the original surface in BL, to the chamber FLOOR
units.box: ~60 soil rows = 30 BL deep, 256 columns = 128 BL wide; blueprints use D <= 26 BL

legibility.passage_note: owner ruling 'passage ~4' (creature.rs:3763) = 2 BL. Real tunnels are ~1.0-1.3 BL (Gravish 2013 [ABS]); P. badius upper shafts reach ~2.5 BL [FT], so 2 BL is inside the real range near the top
legibility.chamber_aspect: keep width >= 3x height. Real width:height runs ~6:1 to 20:1 [DER from FT]
legibility.warning: The ladder's planned 8-16-cell-tall chambers are 4-8 BL tall, 3-5x taller than any real chamber. 5-6 cells tall and 3x+ as wide reads as a real chamber at this ant size [DER]

common_rules: A nest is shafts plus flat horizontal chambers hung on them (shish-kebab). Big nests add more shaft-chamber units [FT]
Chamber height is invariant (~1-2 BL). Chambers grow by widening and lobing, never by getting taller [FT]
Shape is size-free: the same relative layout at every colony size, so a blueprint can be scaled by relative depth [FT]
Most species are top-heavy: big, close chambers near the top; small, sparse ones deep. Aphaenogaster floridana is the exception [FT]
Ants and brood are densest in the deepest chambers; foragers stay near the top [FT/ABS]
A small vestibule or entrance chamber just under the surface is common (Aphaenogaster [FT]; P. barbatus entrance hub with 1-6 side chambers [ABS])
Dug area grows ~linearly (2D lab) or as N^0.87 (P. badius field) with workers; depth grows slower (N^0.37) [ABS/FT]

2D conservation [DER]: in a vertical slice the spoil section equals the dug section, with no 3D dilution. A legible nest (taller chambers, 4-cell passages) roughly doubles the spoil. Budget mound length or backfill for it (P. occidentalis lab nests backfilled ~51% [ABS]; P. badius field ~2.5% [ABS])
mound_rules: Put down beyond the crest, on the OUTER flank, so loads roll away from the hole. Dorymyrmex: 73-82% stay, 18-27% roll outward, almost none roll back [ABS]
Read slope: drop where the surface turns from rising to falling. Tilting a pile shifts the drop point (Pheidole oxyops, 0.46/0.53/0.63 of the pile width) [ABS]
Keep a fixed distance and side: Pheidole crescent ~13 cm from the hole; Trachymyrmex one-sided crescent at 8.0 cm, arc ~75 deg, rebuilt at the same orientation, turned downslope over days [ABS]
Each digger may keep its own dump direction (Cataglyphis, visual landmarks) [ABS]
Grain-sim geometry [DER/GK]: inner toe radius = crest radius - h/tan(repose) must stay >= shaft half-width + 1 BL. At a 45 deg cell repose: crest_radius >= shaft_half_width + 1 + h (BL)
Weather spreads real discs: a 20 cm disc's sand was found >50 cm out within a year (P. badius) [FT]

The ladder's measured falls came from RIM CUTS collapsing the shaft shoulder, not from put-downs (dig-rung-design step 3/4 notes). The literature above is about placing loads and does not address rim collapse

blueprints.name: Harvester stack (top-heavy helix)
blueprints.inspiration: Pogonomyrmex badius, Florida harvester ant: Tschinkel 2004 J Insect Sci 4:21 [FT]; Tschinkel 1999 Ecol Entomol [ABS]; Tschinkel 2015 PLoS ONE biomantling [FT]
blueprints.true_scale_note: Real nests: incipient 29-37 cm (~40 BL), mature 2.5-3.0 m (~300-380 BL). This blueprint is the whole nest compressed to the box at RELATIVE depth (rel = floor/D). The size-free shape is the same at every colony size [FT], so compressing it keeps it recognisable.
blueprints.visual_signature: One zig-zag shaft with wide flat chambers hung off alternating sides. Big and close together near the top, small and far apart below. Reads as a Christmas tree upside down, drawn in thin flat leaves.

shaft.angle_from_horizontal_deg: 20-30 at the top, 45-60 by rel~0.2, up to ~70 deep [FT]
shaft.plan: Helix 5-8 BL across [FT/DER]. In section it is a zig-zag with +/-2-3 BL swing whose pitch grows with depth (8-10 cm then ~20 cm per turn [FT]).

chambers.shape: looping lobed horizontal tunnel-chamber, lobes on BOTH sides of the shaft
chambers.connection: Is a widened near-horizontal shaft; lies inside the soil under the disc [FT]

chambers.shape: flat floor, slightly domed roof, lobed outline
chambers.connection: Inner edge meets the shaft at 25-70 deg. Starts as a niche on the OUTSIDE of the helix [FT]

tunnels.path: the zig-zag shaft through all chambers' inner edges

chamber_rules.height: ~1.2 BL true at ALL chamber sizes [FT]. Legible: 2.5 BL. Keep width >= 3x height.
chamber_rules.spacing: Gap grows with depth, smallest near the top (2-4 cm ~ 3-5 BL real), largest at rel 0.7-0.8 [FT]. Box: 2, 2, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 5.5, 3.5 BL.
chamber_rules.top_heaviness: About half the section width/area in the top quarter. Each decile ~25-50% less than the one above [FT]. This layout: 56% of chamber width in the top quarter [DER].
chamber_rules.attachment: Chambers hang off the OUTSIDE of the shaft's turns, so in section they alternate sides [FT/DER].

surface_mound.shape: flat disc (blanket), not a cone; real ones are charcoal-decorated [FT]
surface_mound.real_dimensions: diameter 10-85 cm (mean ~44 cm ~ 55 BL); mean thickness ~2 cm ~ 2.5 BL (volume/area) [FT+DER]
surface_mound.note: The real disc runs right up to the hole. In a loose-grain sim, keep a 2.5 BL collar clear and a low rim (crest 4 BL) so the inner toe stays outside the shaft lip (section 3 of notes).

scaling_with_workers.area: log A(cm2) = 0.55 + 0.87 log W  ->  A proportional to W^0.87 [FT]
scaling_with_workers.depth: log D(cm) = 0.95 + 0.37 log W  ->  D proportional to W^0.37 [FT]. Extrapolated to 12 / 24 workers: ~22 / ~28 cm = 28 / 36 BL [DER]
scaling_with_workers.chambers: added at every decile, so spacing vs relative depth stays the same; enlargement of existing chambers adds more area than new chambers [FT]
scaling_with_workers.series: 2nd shaft-chamber series from ~3,200 workers (1 series ~1,700, 3 ~4,600, 4 ~5,000), branching <40 cm deep, at the base of an upper chamber [FT]
scaling_with_workers.game: 12 ants: A0-A4 + shaft (~5 chambers). 24 ants: all 8. More ants after that: a 2nd series from A1's base, smaller chambers [DER]

excavated_section_area.method: chambers 0.8*w*h (lens fill), tunnels length*width; 25 open cells per 2-cell ant = 8% crowding [DER]

blueprints.name: Garden-ant farm (meandering branching galleries)
blueprints.inspiration: Lasius niger in a thin formicarium. Dimensions from the Lasius neoniger field study [WS], L. flavus micro-CT (Minter et al. 2012) [ABS/FT via Gautrais 2014], L. niger 2D digging (Rasse & Deneubourg 2001) [ABS]
blueprints.true_scale_note: L. neoniger nests sit mostly in the top 0.3 m (~75 BL) with a few galleries to ~0.7 m [WS]. The whole 30-BL box is the 'upper zone' at true scale.
blueprints.visual_signature: A tangle: 2-4 galleries slant down from the entrance, wander, split, and sometimes rejoin. Chambers are elongated swellings along them. Wider than deep. No single trunk.

shaft.plan: short starter shaft 3 BL straight down, then 2-4 galleries slanting downward at 20-45 deg [ABS/FT via Gautrais 2014 on Minter 2012]

chambers.shape: elongated horizontal swelling, flat floor, low dome

chambers.connection: on G1, where a cross-link G5 arrives

chambers.shape: small swelling at a dead end
chambers.connection: end of the one deep gallery G4

tunnels.path: down-left at ~30 deg, wandering +/-20 deg every 3-5 BL
a loop: meshedness > 0 appears around 100+ ants in 2D Messor data [FT]

chamber_rules.height: 1.3-1.8 BL true [ASSUMED: ~ant height rule from Khuong 2016 roof template ABS and other species FT]; legible 2.5 BL
chamber_rules.length: 7-12 BL (L. neoniger chambers 30-50 mm long at ~4 mm BL) [WS+DER]
chamber_rules.gallery_width: 0.4-1.2 BL real (1.5-5 mm) [WS+DER]; use 1 BL true, 2 BL legible

surface_mound.shape: two-sided ring/crater of loose crumbs around the entrance (Dorymyrmex dumping rule [ABS]). Optional variant: L. niger's built earthen mound with internal galleries (pillars roofed at body height, Khuong 2016 [ABS]). The variant is risky in loose grains and is exactly the 'ants dig into mound' failure

box_fit.inner_slope: repose; nothing new is put on it
box_fit.outer_slope: repose; all loads go here, beyond the crest

surface_mound.second_entrance: optional 2nd opening 15-25 BL away (a G2 gallery surfacing) with its own small ring [ASSUMED]

scaling_with_workers.area: excavated volume ~proportional to N (L. niger 2D, Rasse & Deneubourg 2001) [ABS]
scaling_with_workers.topology: more ants -> more branches and more loops; meshedness 0 / 0.09 / 0.19 at 50/100/200 Messor ants [FT]
scaling_with_workers.game: 12 ants: G1, G2 and B1, B2, B4 (tree, no loop). 24 ants: add G3, B3, B5; G5 loop optional. 50+ ants: loops [DER]

excavated_section_area.method: chambers 0.8*w*h (lens fill), tunnels length*width; 25 open cells per 2-cell ant = 8% crowding [DER]

blueprints.name: Round room that buds (density-driven shape transition)
blueprints.inspiration: Messor sancta 2D digging: Toffin et al. 2009 PNAS [ABS], Toffin, Kindekens & Deneubourg 2010 Proc R Soc B [ABS], Buhl et al. 2004/2005 [ABS], Gautrais et al. 2014 [FT]
blueprints.body_length_mm: not found for M. sancta; Messor generally 4-10 mm, polymorphic [WS]. Expressed in BL by analogy
blueprints.true_scale_note: Toffin's arenas were HORIZONTAL sand layers under glass, so 'round' is round in plan. In a vertical slice, gravity flattens the floor. The analogue here is a dome-roofed oval room 2-3x wider than tall [DER].
blueprints.visual_signature: One fat room at the foot of a short straight shaft. As the colony grows, short buds appear around its edge, and 2-4 of them stretch into thin radiating galleries with small knots at their ends. A blob that sprouts arms.

growth_stages.name: round cavity
growth_stages.rule: Dig uniformly around the whole wall while worker density at the wall is high. The room grows isotropically [ABS/FT]
growth_stages.trigger_to_next: dug area passes a threshold. Lower in cohesive substrate. Values not retrieved [ABS]

growth_stages.name: budding
growth_stages.rule: 3-6 short buds (1 BL wide, 1-2 BL long) at roughly even spacing around the sides and lower perimeter [ABS+ASSUMED count]

growth_stages.name: galleries
growth_stages.rule: 2-4 buds lengthen into galleries ~1 BL wide. New branches start from gallery walls at right angles, at a constant rate per wall length [FT, Gautrais 2014]. Small node-chambers where galleries end or cross
growth_stages.trigger_to_next: digging stops at an area threshold independent of shape and material [ABS]

shaft.plan: straight vertical, entrance -> room roof. This is the current 8-row (4 BL) shaft

chambers.contents: everyone, brood pile on the floor centre

chambers.shape: small round node at a gallery end

buds.positions: sides and lower perimeter of C0; none in the roof (keeps the roof whole) [ASSUMED]

surface_mound.shape: ring crater, Dorymyrmex rule: put down just beyond the crest so loads roll outward [ABS]

scaling_with_workers.area: total dug area ~proportional to N (Buhl 2005: 'almost proportional') [ABS]; logistic in time: exponential start, then a stop [ABS]
scaling_with_workers.shape: the round->bud->gallery transition happens at all group sizes but more often with more workers [ABS]; 96% of cohesive vs 50% of granular runs went all the way [ABS]
scaling_with_workers.game: 12 ants: stage 1 only (a round room). 24 ants: stage 2 (room + buds), maybe one gallery. Graded rather than binary [DER]

excavated_section_area.method: chambers 0.8*w*h (lens fill), tunnels length*width; 25 open cells per 2-cell ant = 8% crowding [DER]

blueprints.name: Carpenter shallow (upturned fingers over compact lenses)
blueprints.inspiration: Camponotus socius, a ground-nesting carpenter ant: Tschinkel 2005 J Insect Sci 5:9 [FT]
blueprints.true_scale_note: Real depth 15-66 cm (~17-73 BL). A small nest fits the box at near true scale.
blueprints.visual_signature: Shallow and lateral. Near the top, long thin chambers run sideways from the shaft and curl UP to stop just under the surface, never breaking through. Lower down there are a few compact wedge-shaped lenses, thick at the shaft and thin at the tip. The shaft wanders.

shaft.plan: wandering zig-zag / loose helix [FT]; larger nests may have a 2nd shaft branching in the upper part (5 of 24 nests) [FT]

chambers.shape: elongate tunnel-like chamber that curls upward at its far end to ~1 BL below the surface; never opens [FT]
chambers.connection: leaves the shaft horizontally, tip rises ~1.5 BL

chambers.shape: elongate, curls upward at the tip [FT]
compact lens; ~1.6 BL thick at the shaft, tapering to ~0.8 at the tip [FT: thinner at outer edges]

chamber_rules.spacing: 2-14 cm, mean ~4 cm rising to ~6.5 cm with depth (~4.5-7 BL) [FT+DER]. Here: 2, 4.5, 4.5, 5, 3.5
chamber_rules.shape_by_depth: upper chambers narrow and linear (shaft-like); deeper more compact; large ones lobed [FT]

polydomy.fact: the average colony occupies 2-3 nests (queen in 6 of 14 casts -> ~2.3 nests per colony) [FT]
polydomy.game: optional satellite nest 25-40 BL along the surface: 1 short shaft + 2 lenses, linked by a surface trail [ASSUMED distance]

surface_mound.shape: no species data retrieved. Use a small ONE-SIDED crescent dumped downslope / to one side (Trachymyrmex rule: one side, arc ~75 deg, fixed distance, rebuilt at the same place [ABS])

box_fit.side: one side only (e.g. the side away from D1's finger)

scaling_with_workers.chambers: 2 -> 10 as the nest grows; mean chamber area 13 -> 47 cm2; enlargement contributes most [FT]
scaling_with_workers.game: 12 ants: D1, D2, D3 (+ shaft to ~10 BL). 24 ants: D1-D5. Extra ants: lobing of D3/D4, then a satellite nest [DER]

excavated_section_area.method: chambers 0.8*w*h (lens fill), tunnels length*width; 25 open cells per 2-cell ant = 8% crowding [DER]

blueprints.name: Staircase shish-kebab (edge-out, centre-in)
blueprints.inspiration: Aphaenogaster floridana / treatae / ashmeadi: Tschinkel 2011 J Insect Sci 11:105 [FT]
blueprints.body_length_mm: 5.2-6.6 across the three species [FT]; 1 BL ~ 0.6 cm used
blueprints.true_scale_note: A. treatae / ashmeadi nests are 7-25 cm (~12-42 BL) deep: the only real family that fits the 30-BL box at TRUE scale. Depth vs levels: D = -10.2 + 8.68 x levels cm (~14 BL per level) [FT+DER].
blueprints.visual_signature: A neat vertical stack of round-ish flat chambers directly under the entrance, starting with a small one just under the surface. Each shaft leaves a chamber at its edge and lands in the middle of the next one, so the stack stair-steps left-right-left. The top pair is joined by 2-3 parallel shafts.

shaft.plan: vertical segments, one per level; each starts at the EDGE of the chamber above and ends at the CENTRE of the chamber below [FT]

chambers.shape: small flat chamber immediately below the surface ('all have a small chamber immediately below the surface') [FT]
near-circular in plan, so a flat lens in section, flat floor [FT]
chambers.connection: centred under E0's RIGHT edge (x=+2); its own descending shaft leaves its LEFT edge
centred under E1's LEFT edge (x=-1.25); leaves from its RIGHT edge

chambers.shape: flat lens, largest (A. floridana is bottom-heavy: most area in deciles 7-8) [FT]
chambers.contents: brood, densest (ants denser toward the bottom) [FT]

tunnels.path: vertical, x=+2; plus 1-2 PARALLEL shafts from E0's other edge (A. floridana upper-quarter multiple shafts) [FT]

chamber_rules.mean_area: 9.5-13 cm2 in all three species -> ~3.5-4 cm across ~ 6-7 BL [FT+DER]
chamber_rules.spacing: increases with depth in A. floridana; here 6.5, 8, 9 BL [FT+DER]
chamber_rules.spread: 'all chambers lie directly below the nest entrance', little lateral spread [FT]

surface_mound.shape: no species data retrieved. Small ring crater, Dorymyrmex rule [ABS]

scaling_with_workers.depth: +0.09 cm (~0.15 BL) per worker; each added chamber ~5.2 cm (~9 BL) deeper (floridana), ~3.7 cm in the smallest species [FT+DER]
scaling_with_workers.area: +0.057 cm2 floor per worker; area per worker falls from ~0.8 to ~0.2 cm2 as colonies grow, so crowding rises 5-6x [FT]
scaling_with_workers.game: 12 ants: E0 + E1 (one level). 24 ants: E0-E2. E3 and the parallel upper shafts from ~50+ ants. A real nest of 12-24 workers would have 1-2 chambers [DER]

excavated_section_area.method: chambers 0.8*w*h (lens fill), tunnels length*width; 25 open cells per 2-cell ant = 8% crowding [DER]
